.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scored/visual/judge.toml and prompt.md (0-5 anchored likert, 'Explicit 0-5 scale' section lines 34-42)
evidence: Type assignment matches the ask across all 27 criteria. Gates: render/authenticated_render (judge.toml:21-24) and constraints/server_backed_local_application (judge.toml:21-24) are binary under aggregation all_pass, as the staged contract requires (staged-task-contract.md:96). Functional: all 16 criteria (functional/judge.toml lines 38-254, e.g. wall_every_route, deleted_and_expired_messages, hold_scope_and_release, sent_once_in_order, persistence) are product behaviours with pass/fail outcomes and are binary. Polish: the 5 criteria (polish/judge.toml:21-63) are each operationalised as a single observable pass/fail property, not a graded craft judgement: timer_label (setting next to the matter title without opening a menu), hold_mark (On hold mark visible without hover), phone_matter (documentElement.scrollWidth equals viewport width at 390x844 and message box reachable), transcript_print (replies visibly set under their parent), refusal_in_place (reason in words beside the form, still present after ~10 s, absent on correct sign-in). Binary is the right type for these, and it matches the template's binary polish dimension. Visual (the craft/degree-of-quality dimension): all 4 criteria are type = "likert", points = 5 (visual/judge.toml:21-73), and every one has a described anchor at each of 0,1,2,3,4,5: matter_sidebar (lines 90-96), retention_marks (106-112), transcript_page (122-128), phone_chambers (138-144). The 0-5 anchor convention with points = 5 and the prompt's 'Explicit 0-5 scale' section (visual/prompt.md:28-36) are copied from the template (template visual/judge.toml:17-70, template visual/prompt.md:34-42), so they are the shipped format rather than a task deviation. The anchors are distinct and observable in seeded data: M-13 has a held message (K-7 hold=true) and timer_days=30 for retention_marks; M-11 supplies the transcript and phone thread. The internal note in 'Internal Quality Checks'!E42 ('Likert we dont use in rewardkit') is the known false positive named in SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170; per that guidance the presence of likert is not flagged, only binary craft or likert without anchors, and neither occurs. Counterexample search: (a) a plausible broken app that could pass because of type choice: an app with an ugly but present sidebar can earn only partial visual credit (anchors 1-3), not full credit, so likert does not over-reward it; a dead polish feature (e.g. reason shown only as a toast) fails the binary refusal_in_place explicitly. (b) a conforming alternative that could fail because of type choice: a good app with a different but tasteful styling choice still scores 4-5 on likert anchors, which name outcomes (clear selection, legible badge, comfortable reading width) rather than specific styles; the binary polish criteria test placement/visibility the public brief implies rather than one exact look. Neither attempt produced a type-fit defect. Scope note: this row is a static format/type check; it needs no runtime evidence. Whether RewardKit's rendered '1 to 5' hint and the scorer's normalisation of a 0 anchor behave as the prompt states is a template-controlled runtime question for other rows (e.g. rubric schema / reward discrimination) and is not measured here; raw-evidence-index.json exists (sha256 6ab23208f1e108aa82388e67ee61cf7496f6b4a6430a748bd602263890395cc7) but was not needed for this row.
